title: Pages in a Stamp Album
description: Open a stamp album through familiar small parts, printed details, and collecting words.
cardDescription: Open a stamp album through familiar small parts, printed details, and collecting words.
focus: The clues describe how stamps are identified and arranged. Direct definitions explain the more specialized terms.
solvingTip: Look for a whole item, a printed mark, an edge feature, or a way of mounting it.
words: Small postal item preserved in a collector’s album
Book arranged to hold a collection
One displayed side within a stamp album
Small gummed strip traditionally used to mount a stamp
Small gripping tool used to handle stamps
Row of tiny holes allowing stamps to be separated
Postal mark showing a stamp has been used
Postal marking recording a handling place or date
Blank outer area beside a printed stamp design
To produce an image or lettering on paper
Planned picture and lettering appearing on a stamp
Set or release of stamps made available together
Larger printed piece containing several stamps
To gather related objects as a hobby

answerNotes.PERFORATION: Perforations make separation possible along small holes. The clue asks for the row or feature rather than the printed picture.
answerNotes.POSTMARK: A postmark records postal handling. It is different from the prepaid stamp carrying the design.
answerNotes.HINGE: A stamp hinge is a small mounting strip. It is not door hardware in this collecting clue.
answerNotes.ISSUE: Issue names a released group or publication here. It does not mean a problem requiring a solution.

title: Coins in a Collector’s Tray
description: Explore familiar American coin names and the parts used to describe a coin.
cardDescription: Explore familiar American coin names and the parts used to describe a coin.
focus: The clues identify denominations and visible features. They do not estimate a collectible’s market price.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a coin name, a surface feature, or a display object.
words: Small metal piece used as money and sometimes collected
Material from which ordinary coins are made
Outer narrow surface around a coin
Raised border near a coin’s face
Broad flat side of a coin
Amount represented by a coin’s denomination
Common name for a U.S. one-cent coin
Book holding a displayed coin collection
Protective container used to display a coin

answerNotes.MINT: Mint names a coin-making place here. It does not mean the aromatic herb.
answerNotes.DIME: A dime represents ten U.S. cents. The clue concerns denomination rather than collectible market price.
answerNotes.NICKEL: Nickel is the five-cent coin name here. The same word also names a metal.
answerNotes.QUARTER: A quarter is one-fourth of a U.S. dollar. The name reflects that fraction.

title: An Album of Family Photographs
description: Turn through familiar photography words and the small details used to identify pictures.
cardDescription: Turn through familiar photography words and the small details used to identify pictures.
focus: The clues distinguish the photograph from its support, description, and camera parts. Some words reflect film photography as well as newer pictures.
solvingTip: Look for an image, a display part, or a word describing what the camera records.
words: Book used to hold a set of photographs
Film image with tones reversed from an ordinary positive picture
One side of a photograph album’s leaf
Small triangular mount that can hold a photo on a page
Written words identifying or describing a photograph
Remembered experience associated with an old picture
Device used to record a photograph
Optical part focusing light to form a camera image
Sharpness of the selected part of a photograph

answerNotes.NEGATIVE: A photographic negative has reversed tones. A positive print restores the familiar light-and-dark appearance.
answerNotes.CAPTION: A caption describes or identifies the picture. It is separate from the photograph itself.
answerNotes.SNAPSHOT: Snapshot suggests an informal quickly taken photograph. The word does not require a particular camera model.
answerNotes.PORTRAIT: A portrait centers on a person or people. It describes subject matter rather than a fixed print size.

title: Postcards Kept from a Journey
description: Browse a postcard collection through familiar picture, message, and mailing words.
cardDescription: Browse a postcard collection through familiar picture, message, and mailing words.
focus: The clues identify different parts and purposes of a postcard. Some answers describe what is pictured, while others describe what is written.
solvingTip: Look for a side of the card, a message part, or a collecting object.
words: Card carrying a picture and space for a mailed message
Scene pictured on a travel postcard
Depicted place or event on a collected card
Postage item attached before mailing a postcard
Recipient’s location written on a mailed card
Brief personal text on a postcard
Blank area available for a message
Side of a postcard commonly used for address and writing
Picture-bearing side of a typical travel card
Decorative strip around a postcard image
Book used to arrange a postcard collection
Object kept as a reminder of a visit

answerNotes.SOUVENIR: A souvenir is kept for its association with a visit. A postcard can be one without being mailed.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: Address identifies the intended destination here. It does not mean a formal spoken presentation.
answerNotes.FRONT: Front names the picture side of a typical card. The writing side is described separately in the clues.
answerNotes.MESSAGE: Message is the communication written on the card. It differs from the destination address.

title: A Model Railway Layout
description: Explore a miniature railway through familiar vehicles, track parts, and scenery words.
cardDescription: Explore a miniature railway through familiar vehicles, track parts, and scenery words.
focus: The clues describe a model scene and the full-size railway objects it represents. Some answers name a vehicle; others name a structure or a size relationship.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a train part, a track feature, or a model-building term.
words: Small representation of a railway vehicle or scene
Linked railway vehicles represented in a layout
Rail vehicle carrying fuel and water for a steam locomotive
Traditional crew car at the rear of a freight train
Rails and supports forming a railway route
One long metal running surface beneath train wheels
U.S. term for a cross support beneath railway rails
Size relationship between a model train and its full-size subject
Track arrangement allowing a train to change routes
Place where trains stop for passengers
Passage carrying a railway through a hill or other obstruction
Structure carrying tracks across a gap

answerNotes.TENDER: A tender carries supplies for a steam locomotive. It is a railway vehicle rather than an adjective meaning gentle.
answerNotes.CABOOSE: A caboose was traditionally a crew car at the rear. The clue does not imply every modern freight train has one.
answerNotes.SWITCH: A railway switch changes the route available to a train. The clue names a track arrangement rather than an electrical control.
answerNotes.TIE: Tie is the usual American term for the cross support. Sleeper is a common British railway word.
